entries.title: Revelation of John 3:1
segments:
Sardis. About 35 miles south of Thyatira; formerly the capital of Lydia (the nation of Coresus), and notorious for its dissolute morals.
 

 
 Seven spirits of God. The sevenfold or complete Spirit, as in

.
 

 
 Seven stars. The churches.
 

 
 Thy works. As the tree is known by its fruits, the works of the church at Sardis proved that it was dead.
 

 
 Be thou. Become.
 

 
 Establish the things that remain. This church must hold on to the little Christianity it still has.

entries.title: Revelation of John 3:3
segments: As a thief. Without warning.  See

entries.title: Revelation of John 3:4
segments: A few names. Even in the church in Sardis, dead through luxury (idolatry of the things of the world) and sin, there were a few who were faithful to the truth they had received.

entries.title: Revelation of John 3:5
segments:
White garments. Emblematic of purity, victory, and worthiness to receive the reward.
 

 
 Book of life. A symbol to express the recording of the names of God's chosen.   See
; also

.
 

 
 Confess his name. Attest his discipleship. See

entries.title: Revelation of John 3:7
segments:
Philadelphia. A rich and powerful city, 28 miles southeast of Sardis.  One of the letters of Ignatius (martyred about A.D. 118) was addressed to Philadelphia.
 

 
 Key of David. Emblematic of Christ's authority and power as a king, because he was the son of David.  See
; also

entries.title: Revelation of John 3:8
segments: A door opened. For all, whether Jew or Gentile.  'Door' is a frequent figure of speech in the Bible text.  See

.  In this connection it may mean a door to everlasting life, or into the church; or perhaps a wider field of missionary usefulness.
 

 
 None can shut. It is possible that the Jews in the church in Philadelphia objected to the admission of Gentiles.

entries.title: Revelation of John 3:9
segments:
Synagogue of Satan. A satirical reference to the assembly of the Jews at Philadelphia, who claimed to belong to the synagogue of the Lord, but were bitter persecutors of the Christians.
 

 
 Before thy feet.  In acknowledgment that the church at Philadelphia was a true representative of her King and Lord.  See

entries.title: Revelation of John 3:10
segments:
Word of my patience. The teachings of Jesus which encourage and enjoin loyal endurance.
 

 
 Keep thee from the hour of trial. This does not mean kept from tribulation, but delivered from disaster in the time of trial.
 

 
 The whole world. This is the first intimation of a widespread  persecution, which reaches its climax in

entries.title: Revelation of John 3:11
segments: That no one take thy crown. The conqueror's reward is to him that endureth stedfastly unto the end.  See

entries.title: Revelation of John 3:12
segments: Pillar in the temple. He that overcometh shall have a prominent place in the church.  See
. All Christians are living stones in the temple of God (
), who shall stand with God and the Lamb on Mount Zion forever.  See

.
 

 
 The new Jerusalem. The city of the elect.  See

.
 

 
 New name. A name in harmony with the glory of the life that is 'hid with Christ in God' (
).  See

entries.title: Revelation of John 3:14
segments: Laodicea. One of the richest cities of Asia Minor, about 50 miles southeast of Philadelphia, and 100 miles east of Ephesus.  Colossae lay 18 miles to the southeast.  It is believed by some that Paul's letter to the Ephesians was in fact written to the Laodiceans.  See

.
 

 
 Faithful and true witness. See note

.
 

 
 The beginning of the creation of God. 'All things were made through him' (
).  See

entries.title: Revelation of John 3:15
segments: Neither cold nor hot. Not actively opposing the gospel, nor ardently supporting it; a state of entire spiritual indifference.  See

entries.title: Revelation of John 3:16
segments: Because thou art lukewarm. Alluding to the fact that lukewarm water nauseates.  This strong expression is intended to show that the self-satisfied and the proud offend the divine speaker.

entries.title: Revelation of John 3:17
segments: Have need of nothing. Riches tend to produce a fatal satisfaction with the things of this world.  See

entries.title: Revelation of John 3:18
segments: Gold refined by fire. The true riches out of which all dross is burned, which shall be a treasure in heaven.  See

entries.title: Revelation of John 3:20
segments: I stand at the door. This is one of the most beautiful pictures in the whole Bible.  God so respects the individuality of each person that He will not force open the door of the heart of his own creature, but stands without, waiting patiently for each one to open the door and let him in.  See
